summary: telemetry-helper 1.2.0 exfiltrates full environment and host identifiers to webhook.site on import
details: On `import telemetry_helper`, the package's top-level `__init__.py` unconditionally POSTs a JSON payload containing `socket.gethostname()`, the current OS username, `os.getcwd()`, and a full `dict(os.environ)` dump to a hardcoded webhook.site collector URL (https://webhook.site/e32d3b8a-a5df-40cc-ae60-7a8343b581e4). The call fires at import time with no configuration, consent gate, or opt-out. `dict(os.environ)` is a bulk environment sweep that in typical CI/CD, developer, and cloud runtime contexts contains credential-grade variables such as AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AWS_SESSION_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, NPM_TOKEN, database URLs with embedded passwords, and other tokens — well beyond anything a legitimate telemetry helper would need. The destination is an anonymous webhook.site inspector bucket controlled by the package author, not the issuing service of any of the harvested credentials.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
